rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; on the zero-tax evaluation, with scope for the failed-election returns. i1116 p. 2, "To make the election, just enter on the foreign tax credit line of your tax return (for example, Schedule 3 (Form 1040), Part I, line 1) the smaller of (a) your total foreign tax, or (b) your regular tax."; p. 2, Who should file, "File Form 1116 to claim the foreign tax credit if the election, earlier, doesn’t apply and: ... You paid or accrued certain foreign taxes"; p. 25, Line 20, "Individuals. Enter the total of Form 1040, 1040-SR, or 1040-NR, line 16, and Schedule 2 (Form 1040), Part I, line 1z, less any tax included on line 16 from Form 4972." Triage executable-triage-v2 (triage/ftc.deepseek.json; 1,228 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 200 partial records): 1,166 of 1,928 comparisons agree; kinds {"candidate-refuses": 456, "candidate-unknown": 244, "project-refuses": 62}; by return {"completed": {"candidate-unknown": 70}, "incomplete": {"candidate-unknown": 86}, "refused": {"candidate-refuses": 456, "candidate-unknown": 88, "project-refuses": 62}}. Both sides now read regular tax as Form 1040 line 16 plus Schedule 2 line 1z (the BUG-0190 fix), so the limit itself is not in dispute; the candidate's zero floor is redundant, since both terms are NonNegDollars and the Form 8978 and Form 4972 adjustments are refused (scope.other_line16, scope.credits). (1) candidate-unknown (70 on completed returns): with no foreign tax (ftc.taxes $0.00) the candidate still evaluates the election conditions and smaller_of(ftc.taxes, regular tax), so it needs Form 1040 line 16 and the answers below it (witness stage10.ira.fully_taxable, incomplete: project $0.00, candidate unknown for s1a.tips). With no foreign tax the credit is zero whatever the regular tax ("the smaller of (a) your total foreign tax"), so this is an answer the source does not need: a model error. (2) candidate-refuses: every one is on a return the project refuses anyway (for example classm.f8889.5.deepseek, gate scope.schedule1; classm.f4952.3.deepseek, gate sa.dependent): the candidate reaches a refused line 16 on a zero-tax return where the project shows $0.00. No tax quantity differs on a completed return. (3) project-refuses, scope (62, all on refused returns): with positive foreign tax and an election condition failed or not elected (classm.f8889.4.deepseek, classm.asset.4, classm.gift.1, classm.retirement.2, classm.s1.2, classm.s1.3), the project refuses with gate ftc.needs1116 and the candidate returns $0.00 (its ftc.h_zero). The source sends that filer to Form 1116 (p. 2, Who should file), which this tool defers; the project's refusal is a cited screen, and the candidate's $0.00 would drop a credit the source allows. The candidate also refuses only on scope.other_line16, which is redundant: f1040.line16 already refuses on it.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope/representation on completed supported returns; i1116 (2025) pp.1-2 lists the conditions for the election without Form1116, which removes that form's limitation. The present disagreement concerns the condition guards, not the min expression shared by both transcriptions. With positive foreign tax the project ftc.needs1116 refuses a failed election condition; on an admitted case both select the same min(taxes,f1040.line16). With zero tax (NonNegDollars), the project returns zero directly and the second either returns zero or min(0,nonnegative regular tax)=0. Stand-alone excluded cases and partial-input order are not asserted equivalent. This ruling does not separately establish the shared min from the waived Form1116 limitation.

Ruling: model error; i1116 (2025) pp.1-2 gives the election/min rule, and Who should file requires foreign taxes paid/accrued when claiming the credit. The reply refuses whenever elect=false, including a completed zero-foreign-tax record where no credit is claimed. The project correctly returns zero when taxes=0 without requiring an election. The bounded source witness .transcription/ftc-zero-tax-source-witness.json confirms the reply produces a model-declared refusal on that zero-tax/no-election case. This rules on over-refusal, not a project value defect or new Form1116 support.
